summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, chronic systolic and diastolic heart failure, complete heart block, and prior infections was admitted for replacement of a failing abdominal pacemaker generator. He underwent successful explant of the abdominal device and implantation of a Micra leadless pacemaker via the right femoral vein. Post-procedure, he experienced transient groin bleeding managed with manual pressure, intractable nausea attributed to gastroparesis and opioid use, and temporary urinary retention requiring catheterization. He recovered well, tolerated oral intake, ambulated without issue, and was discharged home with prophylactic antibiotics, activity restrictions, and follow-up in the device clinic. His heart failure and transplant medications were maintained throughout.
